name: Sefer Ha-Ikkarim
note: Rabbi Yosef Albo completed Sefer Ha-Ikkarim (The Book of Principles), a major work of medieval Jewish philosophy, in Soria in 1425.

book_sections.title: הקדמה — Introduction
book_sections.subtitle: Example English translation / summary
book_sections.content:
Human perfection cannot be understood correctly until we first clarify what divine law is, what its principles are, and how a true law may be distinguished from laws devised by human beings. Rabbi Yosef Albo therefore begins by examining the foundations upon which revealed religion rests. He explains that a divine law must direct a person toward true fulfilment—both in beliefs and in actions—and must lead beyond the limited perfection attainable through political or conventional law alone.

This example is a concise interpretive translation of the opening purpose of the introduction, provided as a model for adding longer translated sections. It should be checked against the Hebrew text before being treated as a definitive scholarly translation.

name: ספר ההלכות
note: ספר ההלכות (Book of Halakhot) — ר׳ יצחק בן יעקב אלפסי. A practical halakhic digest covering twenty-four tractates: Berakhot, most tractates of Moed, Nashim and Nezikin, and Hullin. It removes most non-operative and aggadic discussion while retaining the Talmudic material needed to establish each ruling. The related הלכות קטנות gathers still-applicable laws from otherwise omitted areas, including Torah scrolls, mezuzah and tefillin. The first complete surviving printed edition appeared in Constantinople in 1509; later editions accumulated major commentaries around its text. Placed at 1045 because the biography explicitly associates the work with that event.

A Hebrew itinerary describing travel from Navarre through the Mediterranean and Middle East and reports about more distant regions. note: עץ חיים (Etz Chaim — Tree of Life) — ר׳ חיים ויטאל. The commonly printed Etz Chaim incorporates later arrangements by ר׳ שמואל ויטאל, ר׳ מאיר פופרש and other editors and should not be treated as a single untouched manuscript. note: שמונה שערים (The Eight Gates) — ר׳ חיים ויטאל. note: ספר החזיונות (Book of Visions) — ר׳ חיים ויטאל. A highly unusual autobiographical and oneiric record preserving dreams, revelations, family material, spiritual aspirations and observations of Safed and Damascus. It survives in manuscript recensions and was published only centuries later; 1609 represents the mature period of compilation. Mapped to 1609 from the work's year.

It circulated in multiple forms, including Sefer HaGilgulim, first printed at Frankfurt in 1684. Mapped to 1572 from the work's year.
